subject: Candidate bid: headcount exception & counteroffer timeline
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Alex Zhou - competing offer received / asks for decision window

Karthik / Marissa — quick update on Alex (Senior ML Infra). Mike at Talent Partners just flagged that Alex received an external counteroffer this morning. Candidate emailed that current employer put a deadline on their counter: they want a decision within 48 hours (EOD Thu PST).

Key numbers from the recruiter call: external counter is ~15% higher base and a sign-on of $30k. Our current written offer (draft) is: base $205,000, 15% target bonus, 0.25% RSU (4y). Recruiter asked if we can escalate a sign-on or small base bump to keep the candidate — Alex is enthusiastic about Redwood and the role; this is timing-sensitive.

Attachments: offer_draft_AlexZhou_v1.pdf (draft), comp-band-L4-2026.pdf

Ask: can we approve either (a) an additional $20k sign-on + 6-month accelerated review, or (b) a $10k base bump (one-level discretionary exception)? Need decision direction by EOD Thu to keep momentum.

Laura
Senior Technical Recruiter
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Alex Zhou - competing offer received / asks for decision window

Thanks Laura — important to keep him. A few data points for ops/finance: what's the target comp band midpoint for L4 SRE/ML Infra? Is $205k base the midpoint or below? We need to understand runway for sign-on + base bump.

High level reaction: I'm comfortable with a one-time sign-on up to $25k if we can justify on retention risk, and I can authorize an accelerated review at 6 months with potential merit increase tied to deliverables. A base bump > $10k would require a compensation exception sign-off.

Marissa / Steph — please confirm if a $25k sign-on is OK against budget and whether we need a formal headcount/comp exception to offer a $10k+ base increase. If there's friction, I'll approve the $25k sign-on to move fast.

-Karthik
Head of Platform Engineering
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:39:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Alex Zhou - competing offer received / asks for decision window

Looping in compensation & finance (fyi) — short answer: $25k sign-on is plausible from a budget standpoint for this role and region, but if you want a permanent base bump >$10k we'll need an exception routed through People Ops + Finance and approval from hiring budget owner.

If you decide to go sign-on route, please confirm the structure: sign-on paid over 12 months? lump-sum? Also confirm equity refresh cadence/amount if we want to be more aggressive.

I can expedite the comp exception paperwork if you choose the base route, but it will take 24–48 hours to finalize. Given the candidate deadline, sign-on + accelerated review is the faster path.

Marissa
VP, People Ops
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Zhou <alex.z@example.com>, Mike Hart <mike@talentpartners.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Offer from Redwood — next steps

Alex / Mike — quick note to acknowledge receipt and that I have escalated internally. Appreciate the transparency about the competing timeline. I do want to preserve the relationship either way — here's what I can promise within the next 24 hours: a formal confirmation of whether we can (a) add a $25,000 sign-on, paid in two installments (30/60 days post-start), plus an accelerated performance review at 6 months, or (b) offer a one-time $10k base bump (pending comp exception paperwork).

Which would you prefer if both are available? We can move fast on sign-on whereas the base increase will take additional approvals.

Laura
From: Alex Zhou <alex.z@example.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Hart <mike@talentpartners.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Offer from Redwood — next steps

Thanks, Laura — appreciate you escalating. I talked it over with my family overnight. My preference would be the base bump if possible (gives more long-term confidence), but I understand timelines. If the base bump isn't finalized by the deadline, I'll accept the $25k sign-on + 6-month review as a second option. My ask: please confirm by EOD Thu so I can respond to my current employer's counter.

Best,
Alex
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Alex Zhou - competing offer received / asks for decision window

Marissa / Karthik — I approve the $25k sign-on paid as 50% at first payroll and 50% at 60 days. We should also mark this hire for a 6-month accelerated review with a written set of deliverables (agree with Karthik).

Rationale: strategic need for senior infra talent, low additional burn compared to risk of losing candidate and re-opening search. Please route final offer letter with updated sign-on and review note to Legal for a quick pass, then Laura can send to the candidate.

Steph
Chief People Officer
Redwood Inference

On Thu, 12 Mar 2026 14:21:00 -0700 marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Karthik / Steph — if we want to pursue a permanent base exception, I'll start paperwork now but it will likely not be completed before EOD Thu. Given that, approve sign-on to move quickly.
>
> -Marissa
